studies.title: Rapamycin causes regression of astrocytomas in tuberous sclerosis complex
studies.finding: Five people with tuberous sclerosis complex whose brain astrocytomas were growing on serial scans (four subependymal giant cell astrocytomas, one pilocytic astrocytoma) were treated with oral rapamycin at standard immunosuppressive levels (blood 5-15 ng/ml) for 2.5 to 20 months. On MRI, every lesion shrank, and one showed necrosis. In one patient the tumour grew back when treatment was interrupted

studies.title: Efficacy and safety of sirolimus in lymphangioleiomyomatosis (MILES)
studies.finding: MILES was a 12-month placebo-controlled trial of sirolimus in 89 women with lymphangioleiomyomatosis (LAM), a rare lung disease driven by overactive mTOR. On placebo, lung function (FEV1) fell by about 12 ml a month. On sirolimus it held steady (+1 ml a month), a 153 ml difference over the year. studies.title: Everolimus for angiomyolipoma associated with tuberous sclerosis complex or sporadic lymphangioleiomyomatosis (EXIST-2): a multicentre, randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial
studies.finding: The companion phase 3 RCT (n=118) to EXIST-1, targeting kidney tumors (angiomyolipomas) in tuberous sclerosis and LAM. Everolimus shrank them by >=50% in 42% of patients versus 0% on placebo. Together EXIST-1 and -2 sealed everolimus as a disease-modifying therapy across multiple TSC tumor types.

studies.title: Efficacy and safety of everolimus for subependymal giant cell astrocytomas associated with tuberous sclerosis complex (EXIST-1): a multicentre, randomised, placebo-controlled phase 3 trial
studies.finding: Phase 3 RCT (n=117) in tuberous sclerosis, the disease where mTOR is stuck ON by a genetic fault. Everolimus shrank brain tumors (SEGA) by >=50% in 35% of patients versus 0% on placebo. Because the underlying cause here is direct mTOR overactivation, this is arguably the cleanest randomised human evidence that blocking mTOR works in a genetically defined mTORopathy -- which does not extend to mTOR

studies.title: Everolimus for advanced pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors (RADIANT-3)
studies.finding: A phase 3 RCT (n=410) that made everolimus a standard treatment for pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors. It more than doubled progression-free survival (11.0 vs 4.6 months, a 65% reduction in risk of progression/death) with mostly mild side effects. Another FDA-approved indication built on blocking mTOR.

studies.title: Molecular and metabolic dysregulation of lung cancer in developing anti-tumor activity by gambogic acid mediated mTOR signaling: in vitro and computational study.
studies.finding: Computational (network pharmacology and docking) plus in vitro study: gambogic acid is cytotoxic and pro-apoptotic in A549 lung cancer cells and docks most strongly to AKT and the mTOR effector S6K1 (RPS6KB1). Direct mTOR kinase inhibition was not measured; no in vivo or human data.

studies.title: mTOR inhibition improves immune function in the elderly
studies.finding:
Older volunteers took the rapalog everolimus (RAD001) before a flu shot, and their antibody response to the vaccine rose by about 20% at doses that were fairly well tolerated. The share of T cells carrying the exhaustion marker PD-1 also fell. The PEARL authors summarise the doses as 0.5 mg daily or 5 mg weekly for 6 weeks. This is the human result behind the weekly low-dose idea.

studies.title: TORC1 inhibition enhances immune function and reduces infections in the elderly
studies.finding: A phase 2a RCT in 264 older adults: 6 weeks of a low-dose combination of BEZ235 (a catalytic PI3K/mTOR inhibitor) and everolimus (RAD001) was associated with fewer reported infections over the following year, plus higher antiviral gene expression and a better flu-vaccine response. The later phase 3 trial of RTB101 (BEZ235) alone (MAN2021) did not confirm a clinical benefit.

studies.title: Akt/mTOR pathway is a crucial regulator of skeletal muscle hypertrophy and can prevent muscle atrophy in vivo
studies.finding: Akt/mTOR signalling is necessary and sufficient to drive skeletal-muscle hypertrophy and counteract atrophy in vivo.

studies.title: Mediation of IGF-1-induced skeletal myotube hypertrophy by PI(3)K/Akt/mTOR and PI(3)K/Akt/GSK3 pathways
studies.finding: Shows IGF-1 drives muscle fiber hypertrophy through Akt, via both the mTOR and GSK3 branches, in cultured myotubes, establishing mTOR as a central node for muscle growth signaling.

studies.finding: Akt phosphorylates the Forkhead transcription factor FKHRL1 (a FOXO family member), driving its cytoplasmic retention via 14-3-3 binding and blocking Fas-ligand-driven apoptosis — the discovery that placed FOXO transcription factors downstream of Akt/PI3K survival signalling.

studies.title: The tumor suppressor LKB1 kinase directly activates AMP-activated kinase and regulates apoptosis in response to energy stress
studies.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
studies.finding: The paper that identified LKB1 as the upstream kinase for AMPK: LKB1 directly phosphorylates AMPK-alpha on Thr172, and LKB1-null cells cannot activate AMPK under energy stress. This is the canonical source for the LKB1 -> AMPK step that gates the whole energy-sensing arm upstream of mTORC1.

studies.title: Regulation of mTOR function in response to hypoxia by REDD1 and the TSC1/TSC2 tumor suppressor complex
studies.finding: Hypoxia inhibits mTOR via REDD1-dependent activation of the TSC1/2 complex.

studies.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
studies.finding: RAFT1/mTOR directly phosphorylates p70 S6K (Thr389) and 4E-BP1, the two central translational effectors.

studies.title: RAFT1: a mammalian protein that binds to FKBP12 in a rapamycin-dependent fashion and is homologous to yeast TORs
studies.finding: Discovery of the protein RAFT1 (today's mTOR) as the direct target of the FKBP12-rapamycin complex; one of three 1994 reports (with Brown et al. and Chiu et al.) that identified mammalian TOR, three years after TOR was found in yeast.

studies.title: Lifelong rapamycin administration ameliorates age-dependent cognitive deficits by reducing IL-1β and enhancing NMDA signaling
studies.finding: Mice were fed rapamycin in their food either from 2 months of age or only from 15 months, when age-related memory deficits were already present, and all were tested at 18 months in a water maze (20 mice per group). Mice treated from 2 months learned the hidden-platform location faster and spent more time in the target quadrant in the memory test (28.7 vs 21.3 seconds for controls), while mice star

studies.title: Molecular interplay between mammalian target of rapamycin (mTOR), amyloid-beta, and Tau: effects on cognitive impairments.
studies.finding: Revealed a vicious cycle: amyloid-beta RAISES mTOR activity, and high mTOR in turn blocks the autophagy needed to clear amyloid and tau - so the disease feeds itself. Rapamycin broke the loop in 3xTg-AD mice, rescuing memory and lowering BOTH amyloid and tau, with autophagy induction shown to be necessary for the reduction in amyloid levels.

studies.title: Substrate-selective mTORC1 regulation and gene dosage-dependent tissue divergence in Birt-Hogg-Dubé syndrome
studies.finding: Reframes Birt-Hogg-Dube (BHD) syndrome beyond the classic 'global mTORC1 hyperactivation' model: FLCN acts as a GAP for RagC/D, giving substrate-selective (not global) mTORC1 control. Biallelic FLCN loss drives kidney tumors via MiT/TFE nuclear accumulation, while haploinsufficiency alone is sufficient for lung and skin lesions -- resolving the 'mTORC1 paradox' via gene dosage and signaling timing

studies.finding: Dihydromyricetin reduced collagen I/III and α-SMA in hypertrophic scar fibroblasts and improved scar elevation in a rabbit ear model, with accompanying reductions in AKT and mTOR phosphorylation; causality was not established.

studies.title: mTOR inhibition induces upstream receptor tyrosine kinase signaling and activates Akt
studies.finding: mTORC1 inhibition relieves feedback and activates upstream RTK-PI3K-Akt signalling. The Akt activation was demonstrated both in cancer cell lines and in patient tumours treated with RAD001 (everolimus), so this record carries a human pharmacodynamic component, not only in-vitro data.

studies.title: Inhibition of mTORC1 leads to MAPK pathway activation through a PI3K-dependent feedback loop in human cancer
studies.finding: mTORC1 inhibition activates the MAPK pathway via a PI3K-dependent feedback loop. Seen in tumour biopsies from patients with advanced solid tumours treated with RAD001 (everolimus), where the rise depended on the dosing schedule, and in a mouse prostate cancer model, xenografts and cell lines.

studies.title: Suppressed basal mitophagy drives cellular aging phenotypes that can be reversed by a p62-targeting small molecule
studies.finding: Healthy primary human cells run a high level of basal mitophagy, started by mitochondrial superoxide and carried out through the PINK1/Parkin pathway with p62 as the selective receptor. studies.finding: Wnt-induced mTOR activation drives epidermal stem-cell senescence; rapamycin rescues it.

studies.finding: TSC2 integrates Wnt and energy signals through coordinated AMPK and GSK3 phosphorylation.

studies.title: Lysosomal cholesterol activates mTORC1 via an SLC38A9-Niemann-Pick C1 signaling complex
studies.finding: Establishes lysosomal cholesterol as a nutrient input that drives mTORC1 recruitment and activation at the lysosomal surface. studies.title: Lysosomal GPCR-like protein LYCHOS signals cholesterol sufficiency to mTORC1
studies.finding: Identifies LYCHOS (previously annotated GPR155) as a lysosomal cholesterol sensor for mTORC1. Cholesterol binds the amino-terminal permease-like region; mutating that site impairs mTORC1 activation. At high cholesterol LYCHOS binds GATOR1 through a conserved cytoplasm-facing loop, and by sequestering GATOR1 it promotes cholesterol- and Rag-dependent recruitment of mTORC1 to the lysosome. studies.title: The Sestrins interact with GATOR2 to negatively regulate the amino-acid-sensing pathway upstream of mTORC1
studies.finding: Sestrins bind GATOR2 to negatively regulate amino-acid signalling upstream of mTORC1.

studies.title: KICSTOR recruits GATOR1 to the lysosome and is necessary for nutrients to regulate mTORC1
studies.finding: KICSTOR tethers GATOR1 to the lysosome, required for nutrient control of mTORC1.

studies.title: Genome-wide CRISPR screens reveal multitiered mechanisms through which mTORC1 senses mitochondrial dysfunction
studies.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
studies.finding: Genome-wide CRISPR screens reveal AMPK and HRI relay mitochondrial dysfunction to mTORC1.

studies.title: SAMTOR is an S-adenosylmethionine sensor for the mTORC1 pathway
studies.finding: Extended nutrient sensing beyond amino acids to METABOLITES: SAMTOR reads S-adenosylmethionine (SAM), the cell's methyl-donor currency, linking methionine and one-carbon metabolism to mTORC1. Relevant to why methionine restriction affects aging.

studies.title: The folliculin tumor suppressor is a GAP for the RagC/D GTPases that signal amino acid levels to mTORC1
studies.finding: FLCN-FNIP is a GAP for RagC/D; GDP-bound RagC/D is required for the Rag heterodimer to bind mTORC1, promoting its lysosomal recruitment and activation by amino acids.

studies.title: The Sestrins interact with GATOR2 to negatively regulate the amino-acid-sensing pathway upstream of mTORC1
studies.finding: Sestrins bind GATOR2 to negatively regulate amino-acid signalling upstream of mTORC1.

studies.title: PRAS40 is an insulin-regulated inhibitor of the mTORC1 protein kinase
studies.finding: Identified PRAS40 as the missing insulin-controlled brake INSIDE mTORC1. When insulin is absent PRAS40 clamps the complex shut; insulin makes Akt phosphorylate PRAS40, releasing the brake so Rheb can fully switch mTORC1 on. Explained how hormone signals set the exact strength of mTORC1 activity.

studies.title: Identification of Sin1 as an essential TORC2 component required for complex formation and kinase activity
studies.finding: Identified Sin1 as an essential TORC2 component required for Akt phosphorylation.

studies.title: TSC-mTOR maintains quiescence and function of hematopoietic stem cells by repressing mitochondrial biogenesis and reactive oxygen species
studies.finding: Showed why blood stem cells must keep mTOR LOW. Deleting TSC1 (which unleashes mTOR) drove resting stem cells into rapid division, flooded them with reactive oxygen species, and burned out their ability to self-renew. An antioxidant rescued them. A key link between mTOR, stem-cell exhaustion, and tissue aging.

studies.title: Cryo-EM structure of human mTOR complex 2
studies.finding: Cryo-EM structure of human mTORC2 defines its subunit organization and substrate access.

studies.title: FGF21-modified adipose stem cell-derived exosomes promote wound healing by activating fibroblast glycolysis through AMPK/mTOR signaling.
studies.finding: FGF21-enriched exosomes from engineered ADSCs promote chronic wound healing by activating fibroblast glycolysis, with AMPK activated and mTOR signaling suppressed, improving proliferation, migration, and tissue repair in a mouse model.

studies.title: Impaired Chaperone-Mediated Autophagy Accelerates Intervertebral Disc Degeneration by Inducing MIDN Accumulation to Target TSC2 for Proteasomal Degradation
studies.finding: Loss of chaperone-mediated autophagy lets its substrate midnolin (MIDN) accumulate; MIDN binds TSC2 and drives its proteasomal degradation independently of ubiquitination, de-repressing mTORC1 and causing senescence, SASP and matrix loss in disc cells. MIDN knockdown, LAMP2A overexpression or rapamycin each blocked the degeneration - a new upstream route to mTORC1 hyperactivation.

studies.title: Structure of the FKBP12-rapamycin complex interacting with the binding domain of human FRAP
studies.finding: The crystal structure that showed HOW rapamycin works at the atomic level: one rapamycin molecule glues two proteins together - FKBP12 and mTOR's FRB domain - by plugging into two hydrophobic pockets at once. A textbook example of a small molecule acting as 'molecular glue' to force protein dimerization.

studies.title: Ku-0063794 is a specific inhibitor of the mammalian target of rapamycin (mTOR)
studies.finding: Ku-0063794 is a specific ATP-competitive mTOR inhibitor blocking mTORC1 and mTORC2.

studies.title: AZD8055 is a potent, selective, and orally bioavailable ATP-competitive mammalian target of rapamycin kinase inhibitor with in vitro and in vivo antitumor activity
studies.finding: AZD8055, an ATP-competitive mTOR kinase inhibitor, blocks both mTORC1 and mTORC2 (rapamycin-resistant outputs).

studies.title: Overcoming mTOR resistance mutations with a new-generation mTOR inhibitor
studies.finding: RapaLink-1, a third-generation bivalent inhibitor, overcomes mTOR resistance mutations.

studies.finding: Rapamycin-FKBP12 complex blocks growth-factor activation of p70 S6 kinase, linking the drug to a specific mitogenic pathway.

studies.finding: Rapamycin selectively inhibits IL-2-driven activation of p70 S6 kinase during T-cell proliferation.

studies.title: Topical rapamycin reduces markers of senescence and aging in human skin: an exploratory, prospective, randomized trial
studies.finding: A small human trial testing whether rapamycin can slow aging in a tissue you can actually see and biopsy - skin. Topical rapamycin significantly lowered the senescence marker p16 and raised collagen VII, with visible improvement in skin appearance. Early, small-scale evidence (17 of 36 completed) that topical rapamycin can reduce a senescence marker in human skin.

studies.title: The tumor suppressor LKB1 kinase directly activates AMP-activated kinase and regulates apoptosis in response to energy stress
studies.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
studies.finding: The paper that identified LKB1 as the upstream kinase for AMPK: LKB1 directly phosphorylates AMPK-alpha on Thr172, and LKB1-null cells cannot activate AMPK under energy stress. This is the canonical source for the LKB1 -> AMPK step that gates the whole energy-sensing arm upstream of mTORC1.

studies.title: Metformin, independent of AMPK, inhibits mTORC1 in a rag GTPase-dependent manner
studies.finding: Metformin inhibits mTORC1 even in cells lacking AMPK or TSC1/TSC2, and the effect requires the Rag GTPases instead. Together with Foretz 2010 this places a large part of metformin's action outside the AMPK axis it is usually credited to.

studies.title: Regulation of the TSC pathway by LKB1: evidence of a molecular link between tuberous sclerosis complex and Peutz-Jeghers syndrome
studies.finding: Asked why two inherited tumour syndromes, tuberous sclerosis and Peutz-Jeghers syndrome, look so alike under the microscope. Re-expressing LKB1 in LKB1-null HeLa cells raised AMPK activation-loop phosphorylation and lowered phosphorylation of S6K and 4E-BP1, while knocking LKB1 down did the opposite. The effect on mTOR outputs needed both AMPK and TSC2, placing LKB1 upstream of the TSC2-mTOR axis

studies.title: The LKB1 tumor suppressor negatively regulates mTOR signaling
studies.finding: Reported that LKB1 is needed to switch mTOR signalling off when cellular ATP falls, and that this requires AMPK and TSC2. Lkb1-null fibroblasts and the hamartomatous gut polyps of Lkb1 mutant mice showed raised signalling downstream of mTOR. The authors proposed mTOR inhibitors as a treatment idea for Peutz-Jeghers syndrome. Published alongside Corradetti et al. 2004, which reached the same LKB1-A

studies.title: Rapamycin improves healthspan but not inflammaging in nfκb1(-/-) mice.
studies.finding: Separates two effects of rapamycin that are usually assumed to travel together. In mice with genetically enhanced NF-kB activity, rapamycin showed no benefit in lifespan and no reduction of inflammaging, yet still reduced frailty and improved long-term memory, neuromuscular coordination and tissue architecture, with lower markers of cellular senescence.
